selection.headline: Claude Sonnet 5.5 arrives on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS
selection.summary: AWS announces availability of Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Its release post positions the model for focused coding and knowledge work and provides guidance for getting started in Bedrock. Claims about lower task cost and faster work are the publisher's characterization, not an independently measured result in this evidence packet.
selection.why_it_matters: Teams already using AWS have a newly announced model option to evaluate against their existing coding and knowledge-work tasks. The useful decision is whether task quality, latency and cost improve on a team's own examples, rather than whether a release description sounds stronger.
selection.editorial_limitation: Bounded publisher excerpt only; no independent benchmarks, regional entitlement verification, pricing comparison or hands-on evaluation was performed.

what_to_do_now.label: Compare on existing tasks
what_to_do_now.rationale: Use an unchanged representative evaluation set before treating the publisher's efficiency claims as an improvement for your workload.

selection.headline: NVIDIA OpenShell places runtime access controls around existing agents
selection.summary: NVIDIA describes OpenShell 0.1.0 as an open-source runtime for defining and enforcing which systems and data an AI agent can access. The post explains placing runtime controls around an existing agent without rewriting it, including restrictions on API operations and protection of credentials.
selection.why_it_matters: Agent instructions and enforceable access permissions serve different purposes. This release gives engineering teams a concrete runtime-control approach to examine when deciding which operations an agent should be allowed to perform.
selection.editorial_limitation: Publisher-authored bounded excerpt includes an AI-generated summary. It supports the described controls but does not establish resistance to every attack, production maturity or measured security outcomes.

what_to_do_now.label: Test explicit permissions
what_to_do_now.rationale: Evaluate a narrowly scoped agent with allowed and denied operations; do not treat the presence of a sandbox as proof of complete security.

selection.headline: Microsoft frames Agent Builder adoption as a change-management task
selection.summary: Microsoft's Agent Builder article focuses on behavior change and a structured operating model for scaling adoption. It says organizations need not create a bespoke plan for every team and describes an HCLTech customer example of a structured change-management program.
selection.why_it_matters: Introducing an agent-building tool is not the same as establishing a repeatable working practice. The article offers an adoption-oriented perspective for people responsible for enabling colleagues to use agents, rather than only configuring the technology.
selection.editorial_limitation: Publisher guidance and customer example, not an independent causal study. The frozen excerpt does not supply quantified adoption gains or the complete operating-model steps.

what_to_do_now.label: Review the adoption process
what_to_do_now.rationale: Compare the proposed operating-model approach with your current enablement process without inventing measures of success absent from the source.

selection.headline: Microsoft's AI at Work playlist organizes Copilot learning around work roles
selection.fallback_reason: The frozen Applied evidence includes only one qualifying primary-window item. This September 25 learning resource supplies a distinct, broadly applicable workplace learning angle; the somewhat newer Salesforce reserve is sector-specific promotional framing with less supported practical detail in its excerpt. The original publication timestamp is retained, not its later modification time.
selection.summary: Microsoft describes an AI at Work playlist in AI Skills Navigator, with practical learning intended to help people choose a Copilot mode that fits their role and work. The source introduces learning about Copilot modes, AI FinOps basics and agents, and emphasizes learning by doing.
selection.why_it_matters: Role-oriented learning can provide a more specific starting point than a broad list of AI features. Knowledge workers can use the resource to investigate the mode relevant to their work while recognizing that the announcement itself is not a completed training experience.
selection.editorial_limitation: This is a learning-resource announcement. The linked lessons were not separately reviewed; no claim is made about demonstrated learning outcomes, exact lesson contents or feature availability beyond the frozen source.

what_to_do_now.label: Choose a relevant learning path
what_to_do_now.rationale: Use the role and work framing to identify a potentially relevant lesson, rather than assuming that all announced modes apply to every account.

selection.headline: Qoder suggests reusable Agent Skills from completed conversations
selection.fallback_reason: This is the sole story-ready reusable Agent Skills candidate in the frozen novelty-eligible packet. Its September 23 release falls within the approved seven-day extended article window; no newer qualifying reusable-Skills story is present. It is included for that specific required topic with the original source date disclosed.
selection.summary: Qoder's September 23 release notes describe skill-evolution suggestions: after a conversation finishes, Qoder can suggest creating or updating Skills from reusable experience. The same release describes collaboration features, but the selected story is specifically the reuse of experience through suggested Skills.
selection.why_it_matters: The feature offers a concrete way to turn a completed interaction into a reusable agent instruction resource. For nontechnical users, the important distinction is between a suggested reusable skill and an automatically proven improvement.
selection.editorial_limitation: Release-note evidence only. It does not prove that a proposed Skill is automatically accepted, correctly generalized, portable across products or guaranteed to improve future work.

what_to_do_now.label: Review a skill suggestion
what_to_do_now.rationale: Examine a suggested Skill from a repeatable task and check whether its instructions actually capture the reusable part of the experience.

selection.headline: n8n introduces agents that work alongside fixed workflows
selection.fallback_reason: The frozen Agents packet has no primary-window candidates. This September 25 release is newer than the general executive-agent reserve and supports a distinct explanation of agents working alongside existing workflows. It remains inside the seven-day article ceiling and is not relabeled as today's release.
selection.summary: n8n describes a new agent experience alongside its workflows, aimed at open-ended or back-and-forth jobs that can be complicated to express as fixed steps. The announcement distinguishes this experience from the agents people have already built within n8n workflows and says the two approaches are designed to work together.
selection.why_it_matters: People considering automation need to distinguish predictable sequences from tasks requiring iterative decisions. The announcement provides a useful concrete example of offering both approaches together, rather than replacing every workflow with an agent.
selection.editorial_limitation: The bounded excerpt supports the positioning and relationship to workflows, not pricing, universal availability, governance guarantees or measured automation results.

what_to_do_now.label: Separate fixed and open-ended work
what_to_do_now.rationale: Identify which steps of a task are predictable and which require back-and-forth decisions before choosing an agent-based implementation.

rejected_evidence_candidates.reason: Overlaps the chosen OpenShell story; prefer the narrower runtime-control article and retain a second technical publisher and subject.
Healthcare-specific promotional framing and named customer examples do not provide enough distinct broadly useful practice in the bounded excerpt to displace the selected Applied learning resource.
Older than the n8n reserve and its frozen excerpt introduces agents without enumerating the promised five patterns; do not invent those patterns.

editorial_takeaway: Separate newly available capabilities from evidence of practical value: evaluate model changes on real tasks, make agent permissions enforceable, and turn adoption and reusable experience into deliberate working practices.
